title: Library cleanup: standardize chart atom variants and responsive constraints
creator: Priya Patel
description: Goal: Reduce complexity in the Figma UI Kit by standardizing small chart atoms (bar, line, dot) into a consistent set of responsive variants, fixing auto-layout/constraint behaviors, and migrating any legacy token aliases used by chart primitives. Scope: symbols under /Atoms/Charts and nested primitives used by Table/Report components. Exclude large dashboard compositions. Acceptance criteria: 1) All chart atoms have a single canonical set of variants (compact, regular, spacious) with consistent naming and component properties; 2) Auto-layout frames are deterministic for child resizing across breakpoints (no pinned children); 3) Deprecated color/spacing token aliases replaced by current semantic tokens with a migration mapping; 4) Publish gated by a quick QA checklist and a design review approval in the console; 5) Release note and migration guide added to Confluence.
approach: 1) Audit: run inventory of chart atom instances and tokens used (scripts + Figma search). 2) Prototype: create a set of proposed canonical variants and constraint patterns in a disposable 'charts-refactor' page. 3) Review: get feedback from PM (Aisha Raman), Eng (Marco Santos) and an accessibility pass. 4) Implement: rename, prune duplicates, fix auto-layout constraints, replace tokens using the mapping. 5) Publish: use staged publish with 'charts-atomic' scope and include migration notes.
out_of_scope: Large dashboard files, chart behaviors driven by runtime (canvas/plot libs), and table cell renderers that embed charts—those will be handled in a follow-up ticket.
notes: Avoid changing exported layer names that are referenced by existing downstream code until Eng approves version bump. Keep a preserved 'legacy' page in the file for 2 weeks for rollback. We will not change visual styles other than spacing and token references in this pass.
